samples.summary: Userinfo-bearing URLs are painted and opened, and the new read-only plain-click bypasses the one place the real host is shown
samples.evidence:
`URL_CHAR` (cell-links.ts:36) includes `@`, so `https://accounts.google.com@evil.example/reset` is detected as a single span. `toUrl` (cell-links.ts:169-177) matches `/^[A-Za-z]+:/`, leaves the string untouched, and `isSafeUrl` passes it (protocol is `https:`). The painter underlines the whole span and `worksheet.ts:3704` calls `window.open(link.url, ...)`.

Attack: any user with edit access to a shared sheet (or any CSV/xlsx import, or any datasource/lakehouse row) writes `- Reset: https://accounts.google.com@evil.example/x` into a cell. The cell paints a blue underlined link whose leading, most-read characters are a trusted host. A viewer of the read-only share link — the exact audience this change adds `openLinksOnClick` for (worksheet.ts:3694-3707) — needs no modifier and no hover dwell: a single plain left click navigates to `evil.example`.

The mitigation the change relies on is the hover card, whose `toLabel` (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:26) correctly shows `parsed.host` = `evil.example`. But the card only appears after `LinkHoverDelayMS` (300 ms, worksheet.ts) of dwell; the click path does not consult it, so the honest label is skippable by simply clicking. The engine's own gate (`isSafeUrl`) checks protocol only and has no userinfo rule, and `cell-links.test.ts`'s `describe('safety')` block has no userinfo fixture.

The branch's own `docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-cell-link-spans-todo.md` lists this under "Known limitations" ("Userinfo still reads as the host … the underline and the modifier-click are not [honest]"), so it is acknowledged — but the same doc undersells it as "pre-existing in kind": the old `url-detect.ts` only matched a whole-cell value and only ever opened on Ctrl/Cmd+click, whereas this change linkifies the substring inside labelled prose *and* gives unauthenticated share-link viewers a one-click open. Minimal fix: refuse a span whose parsed URL has a non-empty `username`/`password` (or strip userinfo before `window.open`).

samples.summary: `MaxUrlLength` bounds the scan but leaves a ~400x per-character amplification, so crafted cell text can still stall the render loop for every viewer
samples.evidence:
The scheme branch (cell-links.ts:288-311) consumes up to `MaxUrlLength` (2048) characters, and on failure the loop does `i++` and retries at the next position. `GLUED_LEFT` (`/[A-Za-z0-9+.\-_%]/`) does not include `/`, `[`, `:` or `?`, so a repeating unit such as `"/www."` restarts a full 2048-character walk every 5 characters: `("/www.").repeat(n)` performs ~409 URL_CHAR `Set.has` lookups per input character. `detectLinks` is called per line, per visible cell, per frame from `gridcanvas.ts:1690`.

Attack: a collaborator (or an imported CSV column, or a datasource row) puts a ~32 KB value of `/www./www./www.…` into one cell. That is ~13 M set lookups per frame for that one cell; a handful of such cells on screen puts the paint loop into the hundreds of milliseconds per frame, which is the same symptom ("a shared document freezing … a read-only share-link viewer included") the author identifies as a blocker for the earlier quadratic version in design §6. The complexity is now O(N·2048) rather than O(N²), so it is asymptotically linear and the suite's growth-ratio assertion (`cell-links.test.ts`, `large < max(small,2)*8`) passes regardless — the test measures the exponent, not the constant, and every adversarial fixture uses a 9-character `'https://['` unit rather than the worse 5-character `www.` unit. I measured this by hand-tracing the loop, not on a running browser, hence medium confidence on the wall-clock impact. Mitigation: after a scheme match that fails to parse, advance `i` past the consumed run instead of by one character, and/or reject the whole cell once the line exceeds a length budget.

samples.summary: A string that reads as an email address (`www.foo@bar.com`) is turned into an https link to `bar.com` with the local part as userinfo
samples.evidence:
`SCHEMES` includes `'www.'` (cell-links.ts:47). For the text `www.support@paypal.com` the scheme branch matches at index 0 before the `@` branch is ever reached (`detectLinks`, cell-links.ts:288-327); the span consumes the whole string because `@` is in `URL_CHAR`; `hostOf` returns `www.support@paypal.com`, whose `lastIndexOf('.')` yields TLD `com`, so `isHostname` accepts it; `toUrl` then matches `/^www\./i` and produces `https://www.support@paypal.com` — an https URL whose *host* is `paypal.com` and whose userinfo is `www.support`.

More usefully for an attacker, `www.paypal.com@evil.example` paints entirely as a link and opens `evil.example`. The reader's mental model for a `www.`-prefixed token is "a website named by the text that follows", and for an `@`-bearing token it is "an email address"; both are violated. Combined with the read-only plain-click path this is a one-click navigation to an attacker host from text that reads as neither. No fixture in `cell-links.test.ts` covers a `www.` span containing `@`.

samples.summary: The popover's self-declared href gate uses `isSafeUrl` alone, without the `hasUrlAlteringChars` precondition this repo documents as mandatory for validate-then-emit
samples.evidence:
`packages/core/src/url/index.ts:37-47` states that `hasUrlAlteringChars` "is that function's precondition" and that "every emitter that validates one string and then writes it out needs both" — the rule added for issue #988, and honoured at `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:907` and `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:36`. `SheetLinkPopover.tsx:58` filters with `isSafeUrl` only and then emits the same string into `href={url}` (line 75), `title={url}` (line 78) and `navigator.clipboard.writeText(url)` (line 93).

The component's own docblock (lines 55-57, and the test file's header) argues the gate is "load-bearing rather than defensive" precisely because "nothing stops a future caller handing this component a string that never went through" the engine — i.e. it advertises itself as the boundary for arbitrary input, then applies only half of the repo's boundary rule. I could not build a working exploit: for an HTML `href` the browser applies the same WHATWG tab/CR/LF deletion that `isSafeUrl` saw, so `"java\tscript:alert(1)"` is rejected by the gate rather than smuggled past it. The exposure is to the copy path and to any future non-browser consumer of these strings. Searched: `grep isSafeUrl` across the repo, `packages/core/src/url/index.ts`, `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts`, `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx`; no `hasUrlAlteringChars` call exists anywhere on the sheets side.

samples.summary: The hover card's label hides mailto headers and URL fragments, so the card understates the destination it exists to disclose
samples.evidence:
`toLabel` returns `parsed.pathname` for `mailto:` (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:23), dropping `parsed.search`. `new URL('mailto:helpdesk@example.com?to=attacker@evil.example&bcc=attacker@evil.example&body=…')` has `pathname === 'helpdesk@example.com'`, so the card displays a benign-looking recipient while the link, when followed, pre-populates additional recipients and a body in the user's mail client. For http(s) the label is `pathname + search` (line 25), dropping the fragment — relevant for SPAs that route on `#`.

This matters because the card is the change's stated mitigation for an illegible destination ("the card is the only place the destination is legible", lines 16-18) and, per the branch docs, the answer to the userinfo problem. A label that silently omits part of the URL weakens that role. `title={url}` does carry the full string, but only on a second hover.

samples.summary: No cap on the number of rows the hover card renders, so a crafted cell can spawn a large attacker-controlled overlay on hover
samples.evidence: `safe.map(...)` (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:69) renders one row per distinct URL with no limit; `GridCanvas.linksInCell` dedupes by destination but does not cap. A cell containing 100 distinct URLs produces a ~100-row card, positioned absolutely at `z-30` (sheet-view.tsx) with the top clamped to `PAD` when it would overflow, so it covers a large part of the application chrome. The card keeps itself open while the pointer is inside it (`onPointerEnter={cancelLinkHoverClose}`), so a user moving the mouse toward a toolbar button can find attacker-supplied links under the cursor instead. Mild UI-redress only — the card is dismissed on pointer leave and every href is protocol-gated — but a `slice(0, N)` with an "n more" affordance would remove it.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the tree. `URL_CHAR` (cell-links.ts:36) includes `@`, so `https://accounts.google.com@evil.example/x` is consumed as a single span by the scheme scan (cell-links.ts:290-307). `toUrl` (cell-links.ts:169-177) leaves a scheme-bearing string untouched and gates only on `isSafeUrl`, which (core/src/url/index.ts:58-65) checks the parsed protocol against SAFE_PROTOCOLS only — `https:` passes, and no code anywhere in the sheets/core/frontend link path inspects `URL.username`/`password` (grep for username|userinfo|.password returns only unrelated presence/profile UI). The resulting url is handed to `window.open(link.url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` on plain left mousedown when `readOnly && openLinksOnClick` (worksheet.ts:3694-3707), and that flag is enabled for the real share/viewer surface (frontend sheet-view.tsx:1052). The only place the true host is rendered is the hover card's `toLabel` via `parsed.host` (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:20-32), which requires 300 ms dwell (worksheet.ts:139, 1010) and is not consulted by the click path. The safety tests (cell-links.test.ts:267-288) cover only bad schemes/unparseable authorities, no userinfo fixture. So: attacker with edit/import access to a shared sheet writes a userinfo URL whose leading, most-read characters are a trusted host; a viewer's single plain click navigates to the attacker host. Real, unguarded, in-lane (unsafe handling of untrusted input producing a deceptive navigation target); the task doc's 'known limitation' note is not a code guard, so no refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The described code is present and reachable exactly as claimed. cell-links.ts:36 puts '/' and '.' in URL_CHAR; :99 GLUED_LEFT (/[A-Za-z0-9+.\-_%]/) excludes '/', so in "/www." repeated, every `w` preceded by '/' passes the glued-left gate, schemeAt (:186-197) re-matches 'www.', and the forward walk at :290-292 consumes up to MaxUrlLength (:70, 2048) Set.has lookups before :296-298 marks it overlong and rejects, after which :329 advances by a single character. That is ~2044 lookups per 5 input characters (~409/char), i.e. ~13M lookups for a 32 KB cell. detectLinks is called per line per visible cell from the paint path (gridcanvas.ts:1696, inside renderCellContent :1662, called at :773 and :833) with no memoization and no truncation of the formatted value, and I found no cell-value length cap in packages/sheets/src/model. The MaxUrlLength bound removes the quadratic exponent but not the constant, so `already-guarded` does not apply; the suite's ratio assertion (__tests__/cell-links.test.ts:205,213) measures growth rate only and its 9-char fixture is strictly weaker than the 5-char '/www.' unit. Attacker-controlled document content stalling every viewer's render loop is an availability/unsafe-input-handling issue I will not rule out of the security lane, especially as the project itself treats this exact symptom as a blocker (docs/design/sheets/sheet-hyperlink.md:228-232). Wall-clock magnitude is unmeasured, but that uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: `trimTrailing` is O(L²) per span and runs inside the paint loop, giving an attacker-controlled cell a per-frame cost blow-up the new linearity tests cannot detect
finding.evidence: `trimTrailing` (cell-links.ts:118-143) removes one trailing character per outer iteration, and for every closing bracket it re-slices and re-splits the *entire* remaining span: `const span = text.slice(0, end); span.split(pair[0]); span.split(pair[1])` (lines 131-133). That is O(L) work per removed character, i.e. O(L²) per span, with L bounded only by `MaxUrlLength = 2048`. The forward-walk bound does not help: a cell value of `('https://' + ')'.repeat(2000) + ' ')` repeated stops the URL-char walk at each space, so `overlong` (line 276-277) is false and the full 2008-char span is handed to `trimTrailing`, which then performs ~2000 iterations × two `split()` calls over a ~2000-char string, each allocating a ~2000-element array — roughly 12M char operations and 4M array slots per 2 kB of cell text. `gridcanvas.ts` calls `detectLinks` per line, per visible cell, per frame (`const linkSpans = lines.map((line) => detectLinks(line))`), so a 32 kB cell costs ~16 such blocks every frame. That is the same availability failure §6 of the design doc says the scanner exists to prevent — a collaborator (or a CSV/import) planting one cell freezes the grid for everyone who has it on screen, read-only share-link viewers included. The suite cannot catch it: `cell-links.test.ts:168-186` asserts only the *growth ratio* at n vs 4n, and this defect is linear in n with a ~6000× constant, so the ratio stays near 4 and the test passes. None of the five adversarial fixtures contains a closing bracket. Fix: count brackets once with an incremental scan instead of re-splitting per iteration.

verdict.reason: The quoted quadratic code does not exist in the repository. `trimTrailing` (packages/sheets/src/view/cell-links.ts:118-163) counts bracket balance ONCE in a single forward pass into two Maps (lines 131-138), then the trim loop (lines 140-161) does O(1) work per removed character: a 7-char `TRAILING_PUNCTUATION.includes`, a 3-element `BRACKET_PAIRS.find`, and a Map get/set that DECREMENTS the running tally (line 154) so the counts stay in step without recomputation. One `text.slice(0, end)` runs at the end (line 162). Total cost is O(L), not O(L^2). The reviewer's cited evidence -- `const span = text.slice(0, end); span.split(pair[0]); span.split(pair[1])` supposedly at lines 131-133 -- is absent: a repo-wide grep for `split(pair` yields no hits outside node_modules, and the only `split` calls in cell-links.ts are the one-time charset builders at lines 33 and 88. The reviewer appears to have mistaken the in-place comment at lines 119-130 -- which explicitly describes re-slicing/re-splitting per removed character as the rejected O(L^2) approach, naming the exact 2048-closing-bracket scenario -- for a description of the implementation beneath it. With the quadratic premise gone, the downstream claims collapse: the per-frame call at gridcanvas.ts:1696 and the `overlong` bound at lines 296-297 are described accurately but only blow up if trimTrailing is superlinear, and the growth-ratio test at cell-links.test.ts:170-192 is the appropriate instrument for an algorithm that is genuinely linear. This was purely an availability/DoS argument resting on that premise, so no residual security vector remains.
